topics.name: Paramount Hostile Bid for Warner Brothers Discovery
topics.summary: Paramount launched an all-cash hostile bid of $77.9 billion for Warner Brothers; David Ellison made six escalating offers culminating in $30/share 100% cash; deal backed by Saudi, Qatari, Abu Dhabi sovereign wealth funds, Tencent, Redbird, and Jared Kushner's Affinity Partners; board fiduciary duty vs. deal certainty discussed at length.

topics.name: NVIDIA H-200 China Export Deal
topics.summary: Trump announced the U.S. will allow NVIDIA to export H-200 chips to China with a 25% cut to the U.S. government; the H-200 is NVIDIA's second-best chip, better than the previously permitted H-20 but below Blackwell; debate over whether this strengthens or undermines American AI dominance and the addiction argument for the NVIDIA ecosystem.

topics.name: Space Data Centers
topics.summary: Gavin Baker argued space data centers are the most important development in the next three to four years citing free solar energy and cooling; multiple guests and commentators pushed back citing dissipation challenges, battery requirements, manufacturing complexity, and 10-20 year realistic timelines; SpaceX IPO speculation seen as related narrative.

topics.name: SpaceX IPO
topics.summary: Bloomberg reported SpaceX plans to IPO targeting $1.5 trillion valuation, raising significantly more than $30 billion, potentially the largest listing of all time; timing targeted for mid-to-late 2026; hosts skeptical of need given strong business fundamentals and no capital constraints.

topics.name: AI National Champions and U.S. Government AI Policy
topics.summary: Emil Michael discussed the DoW deploying Gemini to 3 million employees, banning DeepSeek and foreign AI models, championing four national champions (Google, OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI), and plans for data centers on military land; three AI executive orders praised by Jensen Wong as unprecedented.

topics.name: Foundation Model IPO Pipeline
topics.summary: Discussed order of Cohere then Anthropic then OpenAI for IPOs; Cohere's enterprise focus and $1.5 billion raised seen as modest; debate about whether LLMs will commoditize like cloud infrastructure or retain moats.

topics.name: Boom Supersonic Pivot to Power Turbines
topics.summary: Boom announced Superpower, a 42-megawatt natural gas turbine product for AI data centers, using the same engine core as their supersonic jet; Crusoe is the launch customer; raised $300 million; framed as a bridge to profitability funding the supersonic airliner development.

topics.name: Unconventional AI Seed Round
topics.summary: Naveen Rao raised $475 million at seed stage to rethink computer architecture from circuit level up targeting 1000x efficiency gains for AI; plans to manufacture on standard lithography; $475M explained by hardware iteration costs analogous to frontier lab GPU spend on failed experiments.

topics.name: Creator Economy and Prediction Markets
topics.summary: Matt Kalish discussed the creator economy's dependence on sports book advertising revenue and launched Hardscope as a full-stack creator platform; DraftKings announcing a betting exchange in response to Kalshi and Polymarket competition.

topics.name: Private Equity in College Athletics
topics.summary: University of Utah Athletics entering a $500 million equity partnership with Oatro Capital creating a for-profit entity; discussion of potential monetization including naming rights, jacking up ticket prices, and sponsor logo placements.

topics.name: Vibe Shift in Silicon Valley
topics.summary: Patrick Collison's post about a cultural moment questioning Davos morality, effective altruism, and slot/slop machine dynamics; discussion about whether SpaceX represents a worthy mission but one inaccessible to non-engineers.

topics.name: Meta Superintelligence Lab Criticism
topics.summary: Criticism that Meta's superintelligence lab delivered nothing after a major hiring spree; Meta Vibes video model seen as rushed and inferior to Sora; acquisition of Limitless seen as hardware strategy continuation.

topics.name: Semiconductor Horse Race
topics.summary: Aaron Ginn and hosts discussed NVIDIA dominance, AMD software improvements, TPU as a Google-specific vertical play, and bearishness on Trinium; significant switching costs seen as NVIDIA moat.

topics.name: Eon Cloud Backup Funding
topics.summary: Ofir Ehrlich's cloud backup startup raised $500 million total including $300 million led by Elad Gil from Sequoia, Lightspeed, Greenoaks, and Bond Capital; positioned as AI data management play as enterprises need accessible historical data for training.

topics.name: Fal.ai Series D and AI Media Generation Market
topics.summary: Gorkem Yurtseven announced $140M Series D with Sequoia and NVIDIA; image editing models surprised by surpassing AI video in revenue; Flux/Nano Banana Pro seen as dominant image model with competition from open source and Chinese labs.

topics.name: Brex Fifth Third Bank Partnership
topics.summary: Pedro Franceschi announced a $5.6 billion commercial card partnership; Brex's proprietary Mastercard-direct rails enable global issuance without Stripe or Marqueta; 250 public company customers up from 5-10 three years ago.
